filename: An Improved Methodology to Estimate Cross-Scale Kinetic Energy Transfers from Third-Order Structure Functions Using Regularized Least Squares 2026.pdf
title: An Improved Methodology to Estimate Cross-Scale Kinetic Energy Transfers from Third-Order Structure Functions Using Regularized Least Squares
venue: Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology
code_availability: The code for the PyQG model is made available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6380711, and documentation is available at https://pyqg.readthedocs.io/en/latest/. Python code for processing the GLAD and LASER drifter datasets, running the QG simulation, and estimating structure functions and spectral fluxes using regularized least squares is available at https://github.com/manuelogtzv/SF3_RLS. Arch 6.3.1 (Python library) used to estimate the moving-block bootstrapping (Sheppard et al. 2024) is available at https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html and https://zenodo.org/records/10981635.
testbed_rationale: The paper focuses on developing an observational inverse methodology based on structure functions to diagnose cross-scale kinetic energy transfers, rather than serving as an ML parameterization or emulation benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Standard spectral and coarse-graining approaches require gridded velocity fields and are unsuitable for sparse, ungridded observations.
Nonnegative least squares (NNLS) assumes purely positive KE injections, failing to capture KE sinks (convergences) or non-monotonic spectral fluxes.
Ordinary least squares overfits data and yields nonphysical energy transfers due to unconstrained parameter magnitudes.
Velocity increment distributions are non-Gaussian with heavy tails and extreme events, complicating error propagation and uncertainty analysis.
Drifters cluster preferentially in convergent or high-vorticity flow structures, introducing sampling biases and violating spatial homogeneity assumptions.
extraction_notes: The study was funded in part by the NSF LEAP STC (Award 2019625). It uses regularized least squares (ridge regression) in a geophysical linear inverse problem setting to infer kinetic energy transfer spectra and injection rates from third-order velocity structure functions.
